message.content:
Ты исполнитель в проекте live-spec. Работаешь ТОЛЬКО в рабочей копии `/private/tmp/live-spec-dry/wt` (ветка `fix/2026-08-19-gates-without-push`, снята с origin/main `d899093f`). Никаких других папок не трогай: в соседних копиях идёт доставка. Не пушить — пуш за координатором. В `~/.claude` не писать.

ЗАПРЕЩЕНО, это закон проекта и он сторожится на выходе: пять отбрасывающих форм — прятание изменений, откат файла к версии из истории, жёсткий сброс, очистка дерева. Сравнивать «до и после» надо чтением старой версии через `git show HEAD:путь`, а не прятанием новой.

БЕДА, словами координатора. Набор выходных гейтов нельзя прогнать, НЕ пуша. Единственный известный мне путь — попытка пуша с переключателем `LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1`, и переключатель включает проверку внутри самой попытки. Из-за этого исполнитель физически не видит гейтов вроде `tests-present` до попытки пуша, и каждая такая находка стоит полного круга гейта в двадцать минут. Сегодня это случилось дважды за день.

ПЕРВЫМ ДЕЛОМ — ДОКАЖИ, ЧТО ПУТИ НЕТ. Я мог его не найти. Прочти `guardrails/pre-push` целиком, посмотри `scripts/`, `guardrails/README.md`, `Makefile` если он есть, и любые обёртки. Ищи сухой прогон, режим проверки, «dry», «check-only», «no-push», отдельную цель сборки.
· ЕСЛИ ПУТЬ ЕСТЬ — немедленно остановись, ничего не строй и напиши мне: как он зовётся, где описан, почему я его не увидел. Это лучший исход, он экономит целый пакет.
· ЕСЛИ ПУТИ НЕТ — скажи это уликой (что именно ты прочёл и чего там не оказалось) и строй.

ЧТО ПОСТРОИТЬ, если пути нет.
Одну команду, которая гоняет ТОТ ЖЕ набор гейтов, что и выходной сторож, и НИЧЕГО НЕ ТОЛКАЕТ наружу.
Требования, каждое держать:
1. ТОТ ЖЕ НАБОР, А НЕ ПОХОЖИЙ. Два списка гейтов, расходящихся между собой, — это ровно та болезнь, которую мы сегодня чиним в другом месте. Не переписывай список гейтов во второй файл. Найди способ переиспользовать один и тот же источник: вынести общее тело в место, которое зовут обе стороны, или дать выходному сторожу режим, в котором он всё проверяет и ничего не толкает. Выбери сам и объясни выбор одной строкой.
2. ПОВЕДЕНИЕ ГЕЙТОВ НЕ МЕНЯЕТСЯ. Ни один гейт не должен начать пропускать то, что раньше ловил, или наоборот. Это самая опасная часть работы: `guardrails/pre-push` — не плоский список, а живой скрипт, у гейта b своё ветвление, у h цикл, у g своя функция пропуска. Ничего из этого не упрощай.
3. ЧЕСТНОСТЬ ПРО ДИАПАЗОН. Часть гейтов судит толкаемую дельту (запись прувера, охват). Без настоящего пуша диапазон надо откуда-то взять. Реши честно: либо команда принимает диапазон доводом, либо берёт «от origin/main до вершины ветки». Что бы ты ни выбрал, СКАЖИ вслух в выводе команды, какой диапазон она судила, — читатель не должен гадать.
4. ГОВОРИТ ТО ЖЕ САМОЕ. Вывод должен быть узнаваем: те же имена гейтов, те же строки OK и FAIL. Человек, увидевший вывод, не должен гадать, это сухой прогон или настоящий.
5. НЕ УМЕЕТ ТОЛКАТЬ. Убедись, что команда физически ничего не отправляет наружу, даже если внутри что-то пойдёт не так.

ДОМА ЗАКОНА. В этом проекте закон живёт в нескольких местах сразу. Заведи новой вещи её дом: строку в `ROADMAP.md` (закрывается штатным путём, как соседние), строку в `TEST_MATRIX.md`, тесты под `tests/`, и назови её там, где перечислены проверки, если такое место есть. Форму бери у соседей, не изобретай.

ДОКАЗАТЕЛЬСТВО. Тест должен показывать главное: сухой прогон и настоящий выходной сторож судят ОДИН И ТОТ ЖЕ набор гейтов. Придумай, как это доказать машиной, а не словами, — это сердце пакета.
Отдельно проверь руками, что сухой прогон ловит то, что сегодня поймал настоящий: подсунь дереву изменение скрипта без теста под `tests/` и убедись, что сухой прогон краснеет на `tests-present`. Потом верни как было честной правкой.

ПЕРЕД ТЕМ КАК ЗВАТЬ МЕНЯ: спроси `./guardrails/check-push-reach.sh`, какой прогон нужен твоему диффу, и сделай, что она скажет. Гони ПОСЛЕДНИМ действием, когда всё закоммичено. В отчёт принеси ТОЛЬКО итоговую строку прогона и имена упавших, если они есть.

КОММИТЫ явными путями, никакого `git add -A`, сообщение простыми словами о сути.
ОТЧЁТ: русский, простыми предложениями, максимум 500 слов. Есть ли путь или нет и чем доказано; что построил и как зовётся команда; как доказал, что набор один и тот же; итоговая строка прогона; что осталось незакрытым.
ЕСЛИ РАБОТА ПОЙДЁТ ШИРЕ СРЕДНЕГО ПАКЕТА — остановись и покажи мне чертёж прежде, чем строить дальше.

- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — the live-spec push gate (SPEC M-6; scope grown by prover findings F7/F4;
# gate e added for INV-17, the prototype fence).
# Blocks a push unless every gate below passes.
#
# Generic pattern for a host project: copy this file, then in guardrails/README.md's
# "how a host adapts" section swap in your own test command and prover cadence — the
# gate shape (fresh review record / green tests / ownership / coverage) travels as-is.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"
GUARDRAILS="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails"

# -- deletion-only stand-down (SPEC INV-290, ROADMAP row 502) --
# git feeds this hook one ref-update line per pushed ref on stdin (githooks(5)); read it ONCE, here,
# before any gate below can touch stdin — a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and
# must never block on a read. A push whose every fed line deletes its remote counterpart (the
# all-zero local object id) carries no content for any gate to judge, so the whole chain stands down
# by name instead of falling to the reach map's conservative FULL — the fix for the 2026-07-27 hang
# (four tag deletions read as an empty diff, fell to the full suite, died on the two-minute limit).
# This check carries no gate letter: it is a triage read ahead of the chain, the placement
# check-push-reach.sh already holds inside gate b, not a net that blocks on red.
#
# The marker below is the machine-readable half of the convention guardrails/check-prover-record.sh
# states in full: every arm that can let a push past the prover-record demand carries one
# `# STAND-DOWN: <name>` line, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226 criterion 6 must name that same <name>.
# tests/test_deletion_only_push.py reads both directions off these markers.
# STAND-DOWN: deletion-only
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  PUSH_REF_LINES=""
else
  PUSH_REF_LINES="$(cat)"
fi
export PUSH_REF_LINES
if [ -n "$PUSH_REF_LINES" ]; then
  set +e
  del_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-deletion-only-push.sh")"
  del_code=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$del_code" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$del_out"
    echo "PUSH ALLOWED — deletion-only push: standing the full gate chain down (reason: a deletion carries no content for any gate to judge, SPEC INV-290); whatever would guard the deletion itself is unaffected, since no such gate exists in this chain today."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

fail=0

# -- the fast local chain (2026-08-18) --
# The local chain runs the checks that take seconds: the prover record, the pins, skill
# loadability, and the registry and accounting checks. The one slow member is gate b, the whole
# pytest suite, which takes over twenty minutes on this machine and is the SERVER's job — the
# gates workflow runs `python3 -m pytest -q` on every push, in the step named
# "test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)" (.github/workflows/gates.yml). Running
# it a second time on the pusher's machine bought a slower push, not a safer one.
# The old chain is still here and still reachable: LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 runs gate b locally
# exactly as before, reach-scoped, with its suite-budget arm. That is the flag for a machine with
# no server, a network-less push, or anyone who wants the old behaviour.
# Nothing else moved: every gate whose value is catching something BEFORE the push — gate a's
# fresh prover record above all — runs on every push as it always did.
PUSH_FULL="${LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL:-}"

# Gate g, pin drift, is the second cost in the local chain: 56 seconds on 2026-08-18, more than
# every other fast gate together. It stays — it holds pins repaired BEFORE a push, and it proved
# sixty-odd re-aimed pins the evening before — but it stops charging a push that cannot have moved
# a pin. A pin lives in ARCHITECTURE.md or in the r5 rule-price page, and points at a file. So a
# diff touching none of: ARCHITECTURE.md, .live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md, skills/ (the r5
# page pins skill rules), the gate's own two readers, or any file an ARCHITECTURE.md pin names,
# cannot have moved one.
# The diff base is the chain's own, LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE with origin/main as the default, the base
# gate a and the reach classifier already read. Every unreadable answer runs the gate: no base, no
# diff, no pin list. The SERVER runs gate g unconditionally (.github/workflows/gates.yml), so the
# guarantee is unchanged — it just stops being paid for on every push that cannot touch it.
# PIN_REACH_FILES replaces the diff for tests only, the way REACH_FILES does in check-push-reach.sh.
gate_g_can_skip() {
  # exit 0 = this diff cannot have moved a pin, gate g may stand down; 1 = run it.
  local base changed targets f
  [ -n "$PUSH_FULL" ] && return 1
  if [ -n "${PIN_REACH_FILES:-}" ]; then
    changed="$PIN_REACH_FILES"
  else
    base="${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE:-origin/main}"
    git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base" >/dev/null || return 1
    changed="$(git diff --name-only "$base"..HEAD || true)"
  fi
  [ -z "$changed" ] && return 1
  targets="$(python3 "$GUARDRAILS/archformat.py" --pins "$REPO_ROOT/ARCHITECTURE.md" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1 | sort -u || true)"
  [ -z "$targets" ] && return 1
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    [ -z "$f" ] && continue
    case "$f" in
      ARCHITECTURE.md|.live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md|skills/*) return 1 ;;
      guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh|guardrails/archformat.py) return 1 ;;  # the gate's own reading changed
    esac
    if printf '%s\n' "$targets" | grep -qxF -- "$f"; then
      return 1
    fi
  done <<< "$changed"
  return 0
}

echo "== live-spec push gate =="

echo ""
echo "-- reach classification (one read, feeds gates a and b, SPEC INV-45) --"
set +e
reach_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-push-reach.sh")"
reach_code=$?
set -e
echo "$reach_out"

echo ""
echo "-- gate a: fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304) --"
# The reach verdict does not scope this gate (the 2718c69 stand-down, reverted on the owner's
# 2026-08-15 word). A prose-only or scoped diff still sends commits, and the record this gate
# demands is the adversarial read of the pushed RANGE (INV-304) — a thing no file-class verdict
# can stand down for. The only stand-downs that exist are the two PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226.6 names
# by hand: a deletion-only push (handled above, before this chain) and the recordless class.
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prover-record.sh" --push; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate b: test suite green (scoped by the diff's reach, SPEC INV-45) --"
if [ -z "$PUSH_FULL" ]; then
  echo "   the server runs this one: .github/workflows/gates.yml runs python3 -m pytest -q on every"
  echo "   push, in its step \"test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)\". The local"
  echo "   chain is the fast set, so a push here does not pay the suite's twenty minutes twice."
  echo "   Run it locally with LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 git push, or python3 -m pytest -q by hand."
else
  echo "   LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL is set: running the suite locally, reach-scoped, as the chain always did."
  case "$reach_code" in
    0)
      echo "   prose-only diff: the suite stands down by name; every other gate still runs."
      ;;
    2)
      scoped_files="$(printf '%s\n' "$reach_out" | sed -n 's/^SCOPED //p')"
      if ! SCOPED_TEST_FILES="$scoped_files" "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
        fail=1
      fi
      ;;
    *)
      if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
        fail=1
      fi
      ;;
  esac
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate c: every spec anchor owned by exactly one architecture node --"
echo "   Covered by gate b: tests/test_traceability.py already asserts this"
echo "   (test_architecture_owns_every_anchor_once) — no separate check needed here."

echo ""
echo "-- gate d: TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-matrix-reference.py" "$REPO_ROOT/TEST_MATRIX.md"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate g: pin drift --"
if gate_g_can_skip; then
  echo "   the diff touches no pin: it changes neither ARCHITECTURE.md, nor the r5 rule-price page,"
  echo "   nor skills/, nor any file a pin names, so nothing in it can have moved a pin. The server"
  echo "   runs gate g on every push (.github/workflows/gates.yml), and LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 runs it here."
else
  if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-pin-drift.sh"; then
    fail=1
  fi
fi

echo "-- gate f: skill loadability --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-loadability.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate e: prototype fence --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prototype-fence.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate i: shipped-language (no owner name or stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-shipped-language.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate j: no broad browser-kill (cleanup targets the test resource only, SPEC INV-162) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-broad-kill.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate l: muted browser launch (every browser-driving script launches muted, SPEC INV-157) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-muted-launch.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate o: cleanup notice (every cleanup path that ends a process says what it ended, SPEC INV-204) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-cleanup-notice.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate p: touchpoint kind (a surface speaks only the kind its touchpoint affords, SPEC INV-205) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-touchpoint-kind.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate q: waiting list (the board loses nothing — no over-cap shown set, no demotion into the void, SPEC INV-206) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-board.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate r: authority anchor (a decision recorded as the person's names its exchange, SPEC INV-207) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-authority-anchor.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate s: skill review (a substantive skill change carries its skill-creator review record, SPEC INV-208) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-review.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""

if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-doc-rotation.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate m: config health (installed hooks match guardrails/ source, SPEC INV-175) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-config-health.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate k: compaction freeze (guarded docs' anchor map / markers / numbers unchanged, 2.0) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-freeze.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate n: the earned message (an agent's inbox deposit names its birth, SPEC INV-189) --"
# Report-only at push (the owner's word, 2026-08-07 11:19): a deposit is recorded on arrival and
# never blocks a push. The check's judging moment is the intake sweep, which declines an unearned
# deposit at the door. Here it prints what the sweep will meet and the push proceeds either way.
if [ -f "$GUARDRAILS/check-earned-message.py" ] && [ -d "$REPO_ROOT/inbox" ]; then
  python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-earned-message.py" "$REPO_ROOT/inbox" || \
    echo "   (deposits above await the intake sweep; a deposit never blocks a push)"
else
  echo "   (no inbox in this tree — the gate stands down by name)"
fi

# The named-reference presence nets (SPEC INV-239) take NO push-gate letter and are NOT invoked here:
# they RIDE THE SUITE (gate b), the same placement the far-tier report-shape check takes. Their suite
# tests run each net against the real tree and assert the expected result, so a real violation reds
# the suite and gate b already blocks this push. A suite-riding check carries no gate letter, so the
# letter-counting meta-guards (INV-210, INV-212) need not see it and no gate-red-proofs / ci-mirror

echo ""
echo "-- gate h: the four host checks (this repo attached as its own first host, SPEC INV-97) --"
for hostcheck in completeness tests_present traces_to_spec conflicts; do
  if ! python3 "$REPO_ROOT/scaffold/guardrails/check_${hostcheck}.py" --base origin/main; then
    fail=1

done

echo ""
echo "-- gate u: CI mirror parity (every local gate is mirrored in CI or a declared carve-out, SPEC INV-210) --"

echo ""

if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-every-gate-can-fail.py"; then

1	# Guardrails — the pack's gates as git hooks
2	
3	Two git hooks turn the rules the pack already lives by into things that actually stop you,
4	instead of things you have to remember.
5	
6	## What each gate catches
7	
8	**`pre-push`** — blocks a push unless every gate below holds.
9	
10	<!-- generated:count:gate-roster — scripts/gen-tree-counts.py owns the block below -->
11	
12	The push hook runs 28 distinct gate letters today. The roster below is the whole set, one line per gate as `guardrails/pre-push` announces it.
13	
14	Count them yourself, and list them:
15	
16	```
17	grep -oE -- '-- gate [a-z]{1,2}:' guardrails/pre-push | sort -u | wc -l
18	grep -oE -- '-- gate [a-z]{1,2}: [^"]+' guardrails/pre-push | sort -u
19	```
20	
21	A push of this repository is refused where either command disagrees with what stands here. The count decides how much of the tree a push protects. It also decides how long a push waits. It is read against the gate steps `.github/workflows/gates.yml` mirrors, which `guardrails/check-ci-mirror.sh` holds equal to this roster. The roster holds to no number of its own. A gate is added when a stated law earns one, and dropped when its law goes, so neither direction is better on its own. When the count rises, every push runs one more check and waits for it.
22	
23	```
24	-- gate a: fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304) --
25	-- gate aa: doc findings bound (no live document above its recorded finding count; a cleared document stays at zero, SPEC INV-301) --
26	-- gate ad: published tree counts (every count this repository publishes about its own tree matches the tree, and the reproduction command beside it returns the published number, SPEC INV-305) --
27	-- gate ae: named checks (the registry says what each runnable file a skill body names is, SPEC INV-306) --
28	-- gate b: test suite green (scoped by the diff's reach, SPEC INV-45) --
29	-- gate c: every spec anchor owned by exactly one architecture node --
30	-- gate d: TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218) --
31	-- gate e: prototype fence --
32	-- gate f: skill loadability --
33	-- gate g: pin drift --
34	-- gate h: the four host checks (this repo attached as its own first host, SPEC INV-97) --
35	-- gate i: shipped-language (no owner name or stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120) --
36	-- gate j: no broad browser-kill (cleanup targets the test resource only, SPEC INV-162) --
37	-- gate k: compaction freeze (guarded docs' anchor map / markers / numbers unchanged, 2.0) --
38	-- gate l: muted browser launch (every browser-driving script launches muted, SPEC INV-157) --
39	-- gate m: config health (installed hooks match guardrails/ source, SPEC INV-175) --
40	-- gate n: the earned message (an agent's inbox deposit names its birth, SPEC INV-189) --
41	-- gate o: cleanup notice (every cleanup path that ends a process says what it ended, SPEC INV-204) --
42	-- gate p: touchpoint kind (a surface speaks only the kind its touchpoint affords, SPEC INV-205) --
43	-- gate q: waiting list (the board loses nothing — no over-cap shown set, no demotion into the void, SPEC INV-206) --
44	-- gate r: authority anchor (a decision recorded as the person's names its exchange, SPEC INV-207) --
45	-- gate s: skill review (a substantive skill change carries its skill-creator review record, SPEC INV-208) --
46	-- gate t: doc rotation (the pack's split-and-rotated docs lose nothing — every rotated row is findable in its archive and every archive is named in a manifest line, SPEC INV-209) --
47	-- gate u: CI mirror parity (every local gate is mirrored in CI or a declared carve-out, SPEC INV-210) --
48	-- gate v: judges listed (every wired chat judge is referenced in the installed settings.json, SPEC INV-211) --
49	-- gate w: every gate can fail (every gate in this chain carries a known-red proof, SPEC INV-212) --
50	-- gate x: generated index (the committed index equals a fresh build off the body; body and index agree; an empty body reds by name, SPEC INV-258/INV-259/INV-218) --
51	-- gate y: agent card (a live-spec host tree carries its .live-spec/agent.md card, SPEC INV-219) --
52	```
53	
54	<!-- /generated:count:gate-roster -->
55	
56	Each check lives in its own small script so it can be run and tested on its own, pointed at a
57	scratch file instead of the real repo.
58	
59	### What runs locally, and what the server runs
60	
61	The local chain is the fast set. Every gate above runs on a push except gate b, the pytest suite.
62	Measured on 2026-08-18: the local chain took 144 seconds, and the suite alone takes over twenty
63	minutes. The server runs that suite on every push, in the `gates.yml` step named
64	`test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)`. A second local run bought a slower push and
65	no new protection. Set `LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1` to run the old chain, gate b included and
66	reach-scoped. One thing the fast set gives up: `guardrails/check-suite-budget.sh` rides the suite,
67	so a push measures the suite's wall-time only under that flag.
68	
69	Gate g, pin drift, is the chain's second cost: 56 to 63 seconds of every push. It stays local, since
70	pins are repaired because it stands there. It now runs only when the push can move a pin. That means
71	a diff touching `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `.live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md`, `skills/`, the gate's
72	own two readers, or a file an `ARCHITECTURE.md` pin names. Anything the chain cannot read — no base,
73	no diff, no pin list — runs the gate. Measured on 2026-08-18: 103 seconds with gate g, 40 without.
74	The server runs gate g on every push, unconditionally, and so does `LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1`.
75	
76	### Notes on some of the gates
77	
78	The roster above is the whole set. These notes enumerate nothing. They cover the gates whose
79	behaviour takes more than one line. A gate with no note here runs all the same.
80	
81	- **a. Fresh review.** A prover record dated today exists under `docs/prover/` and is
82	  committed. This is the push gate every push of live-spec must pass (SPEC anchor `M-6`):
83	  no push without a same-day whole-spec re-check on file. One record carries the whole
84	  review a push owes (SPEC `INV-304`). On the push road the same check reads that record
85	  against the pushed range. The record names the base commit and every commit reviewed. It
86	  carries the `PUSH-REVIEW` marker and its five fields with values. No blocking finding is
87	  left open. Whether the review was adversarial rests on the reviewer; no script decides
88	  that. `docs/prover/README.md` holds the shape for a person writing one.
89	- **b. Tests green.** `python3 -m pytest -q tests` exits clean — the SAME runner the CI mirror
90	  runs, so the local net and the second net can never disagree on what "the suite" is.
91	- **c. Every spec anchor has exactly one owner.** In this repo that's already asserted
92	  inside the test suite itself (`tests/test_traceability.py`), so gate (b) passing means
93	  gate (c) passed too — there's no separate check to run.
94	- **d. The matrix Reference agrees with the body.** `TEST_MATRIX.md` ends with a generated
95	  `## Reference` table (`scripts/build-matrix-reference.py` builds it from the rows'
96	  trailing anchors); `check-matrix-reference.py` reds a hand edit, a body anchor the
97	  table misses, or a table anchor no row carries, and states its reach on the green
98	  line (SPEC `INV-273`). It replaced the hand-walked coverage checklist at the matrix's
99	  format conversion (row 477); the per-row facts moved to the suite's row lint (`INV-274`).
100	- **e. The prototype fence holds.** A prototype lives in a fenced home (a `prototype/`
101	  folder — SPEC `INV-17`); a PROD file referencing anything inside that home is RED.
102	  This gate catches STRUCTURAL wiring — a prod file naming or loading a fenced file
103	  (a script src, an import, a link target). Narrative mentions stay clear of the gate: `docs/`, `attic/`,
104	  `inbox/`, `JOURNAL.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `NEXT_STEPS.md`, any `README.md` under
105	  `guardrails/`, and `.live-spec/` are excluded, so a journal can talk *about* a
106	  prototype without tripping the gate. If no `prototype/` directory exists (or it's
107	  empty), the gate passes — there's nothing fenced yet. A host that names its fence
108	  home something else passes that name as the script's second argument
109	  (`check-prototype-fence.sh <repo-root> <fence-dir-name>`).
110	
111	- **f. Skill loadability.** Every `skills/**/SKILL.md` parses: frontmatter, name, description,
112	  version (`check-skill-loadability.sh`).
113	- **g. Pin drift.** ARCHITECTURE.md's `file:line` pins still resolve; the named thing is
114	  normative, the line a cache (`check-pin-drift.sh`).
115	- **h. Host checks.** The four scaffold checks (completeness · tests-present ·
116	  traces-to-spec · conflicts) run against the base diff (`scaffold/guardrails/check_*.py`).
117	- **i. Shipped language.** No Cyrillic or owner-name in the shipped set (SPEC `INV-120`,
118	  `check-shipped-language.sh`).
119	- **j. No broad kill.** No tracked script name-kills a browser broadly (SPEC `INV-162`,
120	  `check-broad-kill.sh`).
121	- **k. Freeze.** Guarded docs match their compaction baseline where one is armed
122	  (`check-freeze.sh`).
123	- **l. Muted launch.** Every browser-driving script launches muted (SPEC `INV-157`,
124	  `check-muted-launch.sh`).
125	- **m. Config health.** The installed hooks match their `guardrails/` sources byte-for-byte
126	  (SPEC `INV-175`, `check-config-health.sh`).
127	- **ad. Published tree counts.** `guardrails/tree-counts.json` declares every count this repository
128	  publishes about its own tree, the measurement that produces it, and the pages that state it.
129	  `check-tree-counts.py` re-measures each declared count against the committed tree and reds a page
130	  whose number disagrees (SPEC `INV-305`).
131	- **ae. Named checks.** `scripts/check-registry.json` records what each runnable file a skill body
132	  names is: its kind, its handle, and which tree it judges. The record also holds whether the file
133	  belongs in an adopting project, what it reads on its own, and what it needs. `check-named-checks.py`
134	  recomputes every field from the tree and reds a disagreement. It also reds a skill body that names
135	  a check measuring this pack's own machinery (SPEC `INV-306`).
136	
137	**`pre-commit`** — the concurrent-edit fence. It protects against two sessions writing the
138	same repo at once. It is **off by default**: if no `.live-spec-fence` file exists at the
139	repo root, the hook does nothing. A session opts in by running `guardrails/fence-refresh.sh`.
140	The refresh records the starting commit on line one and the arming session's token on line
141	two (`$LIVE_SPEC_SESSION_ID`, else `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, else empty). From then on, if
142	the commit at the repo's tip ever moves without that session's knowledge (another writer got
143	there first), the next commit is blocked with a message explaining what to review and how to
144	re-arm the fence. The session's own commits stay free. The `post-commit` hook re-arms the
145	fence to the new tip when the committing session's token matches the recorded one (ROADMAP
146	row 572). Only the arming session extends its own arm. A commit from another window carries a
147	different token and re-arms nothing. The recorded tip then goes stale, so the next commit
148	from anyone still blocks. With no token in the environment the fence keeps its old
149	manual-refresh behavior.
150	
151	`pre-commit` also runs two content gates. It rejects a staged line stamped with a future time
152	(`check-future-times.sh`, SPEC `INV-24`), and it runs the **deferral-marker gate**
153	(`check-deferral-marker.py`, SPEC `INV-152`): a work item in `NEXT_STEPS.md` or a
154	`docs/decisions/*.md` page that parks for the human's word — "his to correct", "reserved for
155	his", "still his", "row N reserved" — must name its human-only fact (taste, policy,
156	irreversible, or device-feel), or drop the marker and do the item. A marker that names no
157	reason reds the commit with the file, line, and text. A negated mention ("NOT owner-reserved")
158	and a quoted narration of an old marker are both left alone. This is the mechanical net for the
159	same rule the chat-law hook delivers at the ask moment — the two arms of base rule 29.
160	
161	## How to install
162	
163	From the repo root:
164	
165	```
166	./guardrails/install.sh
167	```
168	
169	This copies `pre-commit`, `post-commit`, and `pre-push` into `.git/hooks/` and makes them executable.
170	Safe to re-run any time — it just overwrites with whatever is currently in `guardrails/`.
171	It does **not** create `.live-spec-fence`; the fence stays opt-in until you run
172	`guardrails/fence-refresh.sh` yourself.
173	
174	## The runaway-child notice — a Stop-time report the owner wires by hand (SPEC INV-213)
175	
176	`guardrails/check-runaway-child.py` reports a runaway descendant a finished worker left behind: a
177	process the run provably owns (in the run's own process group, or under its own temp tree) that is
178	orphaned — its owning parent no longer alive — and burning a full core. It reads no program name for
179	its verdict, only process group, parent liveness, and CPU share, so it can never target the human's
180	own copy of a program (SPEC INV-162). It is notice-first: it reports through the shared cleanup notice
181	and ends no process.
182	
183	This is **not** installed by `install.sh`, and it takes **no** pre-push gate letter — a push gate runs
184	long after a runaway would have burned its cores, so the report belongs at the Stop surface. Wiring it
185	is left to the owner and is done **only when a session is quiet**, because a process scanner wired into
186	a live session's Stop hook could report against that session's own live background workers. To wire it,
187	add a Stop entry to `~/.claude/settings.json` that runs the check when a session stops:
188	
189	```
190	"hooks": {
191	  "Stop": [
192	    { "hooks": [ { "type": "command",
193	        "command": "python3 /ABSOLUTE/PATH/live-spec/guardrails/check-runaway-child.py" } ] }
194	  ]
195	}
196	```
197	
198	Run it against a simulated table first to see its shape without touching the real process list:
199	
200	```
201	LIVE_SPEC_RUNAWAY_PROCS_JSON='[{"pid":1,"ppid":0,"pgid":1,"pcpu":0.0,"command":"init"},
202	  {"pid":777,"ppid":1,"pgid":'"$(ps -o pgid= -p $$ | tr -d ' ')"',"pcpu":98.0,"command":"python"}]' \
203	  LIVE_SPEC_OWNED_PGIDS="$(ps -o pgid= -p $$ | tr -d ' ')" \
204	  python3 guardrails/check-runaway-child.py
205	```
206	
207	`LIVE_SPEC_OWNED_PGIDS` (space/comma-separated) and `LIVE_SPEC_OWNED_TREE` override the owned process
208	groups and owned temp tree; unset, the check owns its own process group and the repo's `.live-spec/`
209	tree. The check always exits zero, so the notice never blocks a stop.
210	
211	## The worker-restore gate — a worker never restores a working tree with a git command (row 479)
212	
213	`guardrails/check-worker-restore.py` reds when a worker run handed a shell one of the commands the
214	clause names. A worker runs no command that discards uncommitted work, in any tree: `git checkout --
215	<path>`, `git checkout .`, `git restore` outside `--staged`, `git stash` and its `push`, `save`,
216	`create` and `store` forms, `git reset` with `--hard`, `--merge` or `--keep`, and `git clean` with
217	`-f` or `-x`. Such a command's blast radius is a PATH, so its damage lands on files the worker never
218	wrote and its brief never named, and the write-set disjointness that fences concurrent edits gives
219	no cover against it. This rule binds a worker in every tree, including its own isolated worktree,
220	since a worktree shares one repository with the lanes beside it and a worker cannot read off its
221	brief what else that repository holds.
222	
223	That list is stated in this section, in the gate's own header, and in `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md`,
224	`skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md`, `skills/build-pipeline/references/delegation-protocol.md`,
225	`templates/agent.template.md` and `scripts/open-lane.sh`, in one wording, and
226	`tests/test_worker_restore.py` reds when two of them differ.
227	
228	The gate reds on this project's own sessions. The transcript root holds the owner's other projects too.
229	A discarding command in one of their sessions is their defect, as row 598 says in words.
230	The key is the session's recorded `cwd`: a session belongs to a neighbour when that directory exists
231	and git reads it as another repository. A session the gate cannot place elsewhere still reds. Only
232	where `cwd` alone answers nothing does the gate take one further look, at `effective_dir`. This is the
233	directory the one command actually ran in, once any `cd` inside it is walked — printed as `ran in`. An
234	owner's home directory (unplaceable) whose command `cd`ed into a real neighbouring checkout is that
235	neighbour's finding too (row 623). The look never overrides a `cwd` the key could already place. An
236	`effective_dir` that is itself `UNKNOWN` or unplaceable leaves the session reading as this project's
237	own, unchanged. The same holds when it lands back in this project's own repository — a sibling lane
238	worktree among them. A neighbour's finding is never dropped — it prints as a notice naming session,
239	directory, command and outcome, and reds nothing.
240	
241	It opens the worker-run transcripts under the harness transcript root (`~/.claude/projects` by
242	default, `--root` or `LIVE_SPEC_TRANSCRIPT_ROOT` to move it): the files matching
243	`<project-dir>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`, one per worker run. In each it reads the
244	records whose `type` is `assistant` and takes the `input.command` string of every `tool_use` block
245	named `Bash`. It reads no prose — a report that merely names a restore is left alone, and only a
246	segment whose first word is `git` counts, so the same text quoted inside a `grep` pattern stays
247	silent. The default window is the runs touched in the last 24 hours (`--since-hours`, `--all` for
248	every run on disk).
249	
250	Every finding says what the shell did with the command. The `tool_use` block carries an `id`. The
251	shell's answer sits in the same transcript as a `tool_result` block repeating it as `tool_use_id`.
252	A call the harness refused is marked there by a `toolDenialKind` key. Its four values are
253	`automode-blocked`, `permission-rule`, `user-rejected` and `interrupted`. A call that reached a
254	shell carries no such key, whatever its exit status.
255	
256	So a finding reads one of three ways. The command ran. The harness declined it. Or the transcript
257	answers nothing, and the outcome is unknown. All three red, because the rule forbids handing such a
258	command to a shell at all. Whether the shell obeyed lies outside the worker's reach.
259	
260	What the outcome tells the reader is how much recovery it faces. The findings print ranked by that:
261	the executed ones first, the unanswered ones second, the declined attempts last. The unanswered ones
262	outrank the declined because they cannot be ruled out. The verdict line tallies the three. The typed
263	JSON line carries `outcome`, an `outcomes` count, and the first finding after the ranking.
264	tlvphotos asked for this on 2026-08-12, in
265	`inbox/2026-08-12-tlvphotos-reply-worker-restore-finding.md`. It had received a finding that read as
266	lost work, when the classifier had declined the command and nothing was lost.
267	
268	It is BLOCKING and rides the verify step rather than the push chain: a push gate runs long after the
269	bytes are gone, while verify is where the orchestrator accepts a worker's result. It is armed in two
270	places. `skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md` step 8 names the command a session runs before it accepts a
271	worker's result, and `tests/test_worker_restore.py` runs it against the machine's real transcript
272	root so a red reaches a person on the next suite run. When the transcript root does not exist the
273	gate stands down by name and exits zero; when the root exists but holds no worker-run transcript, the
274	layout it reads has moved and it reds by name through `guardrails/nonempty_input.py` rather than
275	reporting clean over nothing (SPEC INV-218).
276	
277	The gate carries a counting start, `COUNTING_FROM` in its own header (`--counting-from`,
278	`LIVE_SPEC_WORKER_RESTORE_FROM`). This machine's transcripts hold worker runs from before the clause
279	existed that carry a discarding command. This page states no figure for that class, and no figure
280	would hold. The runs live in a transcript root outside this repository, and that root grows while a
281	person reads it. Two readings minutes apart returned different totals on 2026-08-06. Ask the machine
282	that holds them instead. The command
283	`python3 guardrails/check-worker-restore.py --counting-from 2000-01-01 --all` lists every such run on
284	this machine, with the date each one carries. A finding stamped before the counting start is carried
285	as history: every verdict line counts it and it reds nothing. A finding stamped on or after that date
286	reds, and so does a finding whose record carries no timestamp, since the gate cannot place it.
287	
288	## How a host project adapts the pattern
289	
290	**The ratchet gates (style lint · redundancy · freeze) install themselves in one pass:** run
291	`bash <pack>/adopt/install-ratchet.sh` from the host root (SPEC INV-172). It vendors the scripts
292	with a source-pin manifest, seeds the host's debt caps at the sizes measured that moment — green
293	at once, shrinking-only from then on — and generates the guard test. The section below covers the
294	structural gates, which are adapted by hand.
295	
296	The gate shape (fresh review · green tests · ownership · full coverage · prototype fence ·
297	loadability · pin drift · host checks · shipped language · no broad kill · freeze · muted launch ·
298	config health) is the part worth copying as-is. What changes per host:
299	
300	- **Test command.** Swap `python3 -m pytest -q tests` in `check-tests.sh` for whatever the host
301	  runs (`npm test`, `go test`, …) — and set the CI mirror to the SAME command, so the local net
302	  never under-runs what CI runs (a runner that collects fewer tests than CI false-greens locally).
303	- **Review cadence.** Not every host proves the whole spec before every push — a host may
304	  only require a full prover pass before a major version, checking something lighter
305	  (or nothing) in between. That cadence is a host setting; state it in
306	  the host's own profile and adjust `check-prover-record.sh`'s expectations (or drop gate a
307	  entirely) to match.
308	- **File names/paths.** If the host's matrix or prover folder lives somewhere else, pass
309	  it as the script's argument, or edit the default.
310	- **Fence home name.** If the host calls its prototype home something other than
311	  `prototype/` (say `sketches/` or `labs/`), pass that name as
312	  `check-prototype-fence.sh`'s second argument instead of renaming the script.
313	
314	Everything else — the fence being opt-in, the plain-English failure messages, hooks
315	living in a version-controlled `guardrails/` folder rather than only inside `.git/hooks/`
316	so they travel with the repo — is meant to hold for any host.
317	
318	## The gate contract (SPEC INV-47)
319	
320	A gate born from a stated law scans the WHOLE tracked tree, retroactive by construction (SPEC
321	INV-176) — never only the diff. Pre-gate debt surfaces the day the gate lands; a backlog too
322	large to fold at once is absorbed by seeding the cap at the current size (SPEC INV-172).
323	
324	Every gate script authored or next touched in this directory obeys three conventions (the
325	neighbours' CLI lesson, adopted from OpenSpec's gate contract — provenance and the full
326	borrowings inventory: docs/research/2026-07-10-originality-audit.md; the adopting row rests in
327	the queue archive):
328	
329	1. **A blocking red carries one typed line.** Beside its human lines, a BLOCKING gate that fails
330	   emits exactly one parseable JSON object — `{"severity": "...", "code": "...", "message": "...",
331	   "fix": "..."}` — where `fix` is the same sentence a person reads. Agents parse the line; humans
332	   read the prose; both see one truth. (First gate under the contract: `check-prototype-fence.sh`.)
333	2. **Every check declares blocking or advisory.** A header comment names it; an advisory check
334	   prints its findings and never flips the exit code.
335	3. **All-or-nothing writes.** A script that rebuilds artifacts validates every output before writing any — no half-written artifact ever lands on disk.
336	
337	Exempt by name: `check-push-reach.sh` — its exit code is a VERDICT (which checks the diff can
338	reach) rather than a defect; it is a decider, informational rather than a blocking gate.
339	
340	## The CI mirror (SPEC M-5, ROADMAP row 14)
341	
342	The gates' native home is the LOCAL pre-push hook — CI is the second net, never the first. Three
343	rules: **same checks, one source of truth** — CI invokes the same scripts in this directory
344	and never redefines a check; **the full set, always** — the reach map (SPEC INV-45) is a local latency
345	optimization, the second net stays conservative; **a plain workflow a host copies** — swap the test
346	command for your own, keep the script calls. The worked example is this repo's own
347	`.github/workflows/gates.yml` (note its `fetch-depth: 0` — the prover-record freshness rule reads
348	history — and its `TZ` pin, so "today" is measured in the author's own timezone, distinct from UTC).
349	
350	## The kill-list scanner (SPEC E-26)
351	
352	A host with taste-reviewed artifacts keeps a kill-list beside them (template:
353	`templates/KILL_LIST.template.md` — the human's cuts as dated literals, appended, never removed) and
354	wires a SCANNER: a test that reads the kill-list table and greps the artifact's surfaces for each
355	literal — a killed phrase reappearing turns the suite red. Same shape as every gate here: the list is the
356	declared truth, the test re-walks it every run.

# Guardrails — the pack's gates as git hooks

Two git hooks turn the rules the pack already lives by into things that actually stop you,
instead of things you have to remember.

## What each gate catches

**`pre-push`** — blocks a push unless every gate below holds.

<!-- generated:count:gate-roster — scripts/gen-tree-counts.py owns the block below -->

The push hook runs 28 distinct gate letters today. The roster below is the whole set, one line per gate as `guardrails/pre-push` announces it.

Count them yourself, and list them:

```
grep -oE -- '-- gate [a-z]{1,2}:' guardrails/pre-push | sort -u | wc -l
grep -oE -- '-- gate [a-z]{1,2}: [^"]+' guardrails/pre-push | sort -u
```

A push of this repository is refused where either command disagrees with what stands here. The count decides how much of the tree a push protects. It also decides how long a push waits. It is read against the gate steps `.github/workflows/gates.yml` mirrors, which `guardrails/check-ci-mirror.sh` holds equal to this roster. The roster holds to no number of its own. A gate is added when a stated law earns one, and dropped when its law goes, so neither direction is better on its own. When the count rises, every push runs one more check and waits for it.

```
-- gate a: fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304) --
-- gate aa: doc findings bound (no live document above its recorded finding count; a cleared document stays at zero, SPEC INV-301) --
-- gate ad: published tree counts (every count this repository publishes about its own tree matches the tree, and the reproduction command beside it returns the published number, SPEC INV-305) --
-- gate ae: named checks (the registry says what each runnable file a skill body names is, SPEC INV-306) --
-- gate b: test suite green (scoped by the diff's reach, SPEC INV-45) --
-- gate c: every spec anchor owned by exactly one architecture node --
-- gate d: TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218) --
-- gate e: prototype fence --
-- gate f: skill loadability --
-- gate g: pin drift --
-- gate h: the four host checks (this repo attached as its own first host, SPEC INV-97) --
-- gate i: shipped-language (no owner name or stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120) --
-- gate j: no broad browser-kill (cleanup targets the test resource only, SPEC INV-162) --
-- gate k: compaction freeze (guarded docs' anchor map / markers / numbers unchanged, 2.0) --
-- gate l: muted browser launch (every browser-driving script launches muted, SPEC INV-157) --
-- gate m: config health (installed hooks match guardrails/ source, SPEC INV-175) --
-- gate n: the earned message (an agent's inbox deposit names its birth, SPEC INV-189) --
-- gate o: cleanup notice (every cleanup path that ends a process says what it ended, SPEC INV-204) --
-- gate p: touchpoint kind (a surface speaks only the kind its touchpoint affords, SPEC INV-205) --
-- gate q: waiting list (the board loses nothing — no over-cap shown set, no demotion into the void, SPEC INV-206) --
-- gate r: authority anchor (a decision recorded as the person's names its exchange, SPEC INV-207) --
-- gate s: skill review (a substantive skill change carries its skill-creator review record, SPEC INV-208) --
-- gate t: doc rotation (the pack's split-and-rotated docs lose nothing — every rotated row is findable in its archive and every archive is named in a manifest line, SPEC INV-209) --
-- gate u: CI mirror parity (every local gate is mirrored in CI or a declared carve-out, SPEC INV-210) --
-- gate v: judges listed (every wired chat judge is referenced in the installed settings.json, SPEC INV-211) --
-- gate w: every gate can fail (every gate in this chain carries a known-red proof, SPEC INV-212) --
-- gate x: generated index (the committed index equals a fresh build off the body; body and index agree; an empty body reds by name, SPEC INV-258/INV-259/INV-218) --
-- gate y: agent card (a live-spec host tree carries its .live-spec/agent.md card, SPEC INV-219) --
```

<!-- /generated:count:gate-roster -->

Each check lives in its own small script so it can be run and tested on its own, pointed at a
scratch file instead of the real repo.

### What runs locally, and what the server runs

The local chain is the fast set. Every gate above runs on a push except gate b, the pytest suite.
Measured on 2026-08-18: the local chain took 144 seconds, and the suite alone takes over twenty
minutes. The server runs that suite on every push, in the `gates.yml` step named
`test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)`. A second local run bought a slower push and
no new protection. Set `LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1` to run the old chain, gate b included and
reach-scoped. One thing the fast set gives up: `guardrails/check-suite-budget.sh` rides the suite,
so a push measures the suite's wall-time only under that flag.

Gate g, pin drift, is the chain's second cost: 56 to 63 seconds of every push. It stays local, since
pins are repaired because it stands there. It now runs only when the push can move a pin. That means
a diff touching `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `.live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md`, `skills/`, the gate's
own two readers, or a file an `ARCHITECTURE.md` pin names. Anything the chain cannot read — no base,
no diff, no pin list — runs the gate. Measured on 2026-08-18: 103 seconds with gate g, 40 without.
The server runs gate g on every push, unconditionally, and so does `LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1`.

### Notes on some of the gates

The roster above is the whole set. These notes enumerate nothing. They cover the gates whose
behaviour takes more than one line. A gate with no note here runs all the same.

- **a. Fresh review.** A prover record dated today exists under `docs/prover/` and is
  committed. This is the push gate every push of live-spec must pass (SPEC anchor `M-6`):
  no push without a same-day whole-spec re-check on file. One record carries the whole
  review a push owes (SPEC `INV-304`). On the push road the same check reads that record
  against the pushed range. The record names the base commit and every commit reviewed. It
  carries the `PUSH-REVIEW` marker and its five fields with values. No blocking finding is
  left open. Whether the review was adversarial rests on the reviewer; no script decides
  that. `docs/prover/README.md` holds the shape for a person writing one.
- **b. Tests green.** `python3 -m pytest -q tests` exits clean — the SAME runner the CI mirror
  runs, so the local net and the second net can never disagree on what "the suite" is.
- **c. Every spec anchor has exactly one owner.** In this repo that's already asserted
  inside the test suite itself (`tests/test_traceability.py`), so gate (b) passing means
  gate (c) passed too — there's no separate check to run.
- **d. The matrix Reference agrees with the body.** `TEST_MATRIX.md` ends with a generated
  `## Reference` table (`scripts/build-matrix-reference.py` builds it from the rows'
  trailing anchors); `check-matrix-reference.py` reds a hand edit, a body anchor the
  table misses, or a table anchor no row carries, and states its reach on the green
  line (SPEC `INV-273`). It replaced the hand-walked coverage checklist at the matrix's
  format conversion (row 477); the per-row facts moved to the suite's row lint (`INV-274`).
- **e. The prototype fence holds.** A prototype lives in a fenced home (a `prototype/`
  folder — SPEC `INV-17`); a PROD file referencing anything inside that home is RED.
  This gate catches STRUCTURAL wiring — a prod file naming or loading a fenced file
  (a script src, an import, a link target). Narrative mentions stay clear of the gate: `docs/`, `attic/`,
  `inbox/`, `JOURNAL.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `NEXT_STEPS.md`, any `README.md` under
  `guardrails/`, and `.live-spec/` are excluded, so a journal can talk *about* a
  prototype without tripping the gate. If no `prototype/` directory exists (or it's
  empty), the gate passes — there's nothing fenced yet. A host that names its fence
  home something else passes that name as the script's second argument
  (`check-prototype-fence.sh <repo-root> <fence-dir-name>`).

- **f. Skill loadability.** Every `skills/**/SKILL.md` parses: frontmatter, name, description,
  version (`check-skill-loadability.sh`).
- **g. Pin drift.** ARCHITECTURE.md's `file:line` pins still resolve; the named thing is
  normative, the line a cache (`check-pin-drift.sh`).
- **h. Host checks.** The four scaffold checks (completeness · tests-present ·
  traces-to-spec · conflicts) run against the base diff (`scaffold/guardrails/check_*.py`).
- **i. Shipped language.** No Cyrillic or owner-name in the shipped set (SPEC `INV-120`,
  `check-shipped-language.sh`).
- **j. No broad kill.** No tracked script name-kills a browser broadly (SPEC `INV-162`,
  `check-broad-kill.sh`).
- **k. Freeze.** Guarded docs match their compaction baseline where one is armed
  (`check-freeze.sh`).
- **l. Muted launch.** Every browser-driving script launches muted (SPEC `INV-157`,
  `check-muted-launch.sh`).
- **m. Config health.** The installed hooks match their `guardrails/` sources byte-for-byte
  (SPEC `INV-175`, `check-config-health.sh`).
- **ad. Published tree counts.** `guardrails/tree-counts.json` declares every count this repository
  publishes about its own tree, the measurement that produces it, and the pages that state it.
  `check-tree-counts.py` re-measures each declared count against the committed tree and reds a page
  whose number disagrees (SPEC `INV-305`).
- **ae. Named checks.** `scripts/check-registry.json` records what each runnable file a skill body
  names is: its kind, its handle, and which tree it judges. The record also holds whether the file
  belongs in an adopting project, what it reads on its own, and what it needs. `check-named-checks.py`
  recomputes every field from the tree and reds a disagreement. It also reds a skill body that names
  a check measuring this pack's own machinery (SPEC `INV-306`).

**`pre-commit`** — the concurrent-edit fence. It protects against two sessions writing the
same repo at once. It is **off by default**: if no `.live-spec-fence` file exists at the
repo root, the hook does nothing. A session opts in by running `guardrails/fence-refresh.sh`.
The refresh records the starting commit on line one and the arming session's token on line
two (`$LIVE_SPEC_SESSION_ID`, else `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, else empty). From then on, if
the commit at the repo's tip ever moves without that session's knowledge (another writer got
there first), the next commit is blocked with a message explaining what to review and how to
re-arm the fence. The session's own commits stay free. The `post-commit` hook re-arms the
fence to the new tip when the committing session's token matches the recorded one (ROADMAP
row 572). Only the arming session extends its own arm. A commit from another window carries a
different token and re-arms nothing. The recorded tip then goes stale, so the next commit
from anyone still blocks. With no token in the environment the fence keeps its old
manual-refresh behavior.

`pre-commit` also runs two content gates. It rejects a staged line stamped with a future time
(`check-future-times.sh`, SPEC `INV-24`), and it runs the **deferral-marker gate**
(`check-deferral-marker.py`, SPEC `INV-152`): a work item in `NEXT_STEPS.md` or a
`docs/decisions/*.md` page that parks for the human's word — "his to correct", "reserved for
his", "still his", "row N reserved" — must name its human-only fact (taste, policy,
irreversible, or device-feel), or drop the marker and do the item. A marker that names no
reason reds the commit with the file, line, and text. A negated mention ("NOT owner-reserved")
and a quoted narration of an old marker are both left alone. This is the mechanical net for the
same rule the chat-law hook delivers at the ask moment — the two arms of base rule 29.

## How to install

From the repo root:

```
./guardrails/install.sh
```

This copies `pre-commit`, `post-commit`, and `pre-push` into `.git/hooks/` and makes them executable.
Safe to re-run any time — it just overwrites with whatever is currently in `guardrails/`.
It does **not** create `.live-spec-fence`; the fence stays opt-in until you run
`guardrails/fence-refresh.sh` yourself.

## The runaway-child notice — a Stop-time report the owner wires by hand (SPEC INV-213)

`guardrails/check-runaway-child.py` reports a runaway descendant a finished worker left behind: a
process the run provably owns (in the run's own process group, or under its own temp tree) that is
orphaned — its owning parent no longer alive — and burning a full core. It reads no program name for
its verdict, only process group, parent liveness, and CPU share, so it can never target the human's
own copy of a program (SPEC INV-162). It is notice-first: it reports through the shared cleanup notice
and ends no process.

This is **not** installed by `install.sh`, and it takes **no** pre-push gate letter — a push gate runs
long after a runaway would have burned its cores, so the report belongs at the Stop surface. Wiring it
is left to the owner and is done **only when a session is quiet**, because a process scanner wired into
a live session's Stop hook could report against that session's own live background workers. To wire it,
add a Stop entry to `~/.claude/settings.json` that runs the check when a session stops:

```
"hooks": {
  "Stop": [
    { "hooks": [ { "type": "command",
        "command": "python3 /ABSOLUTE/PATH/live-spec/guardrails/check-runaway-child.py" } ] }
  ]
}
```

Run it against a simulated table first to see its shape without touching the real process list:

```
LIVE_SPEC_RUNAWAY_PROCS_JSON='[{"pid":1,"ppid":0,"pgid":1,"pcpu":0.0,"command":"init"},
  {"pid":777,"ppid":1,"pgid":'"$(ps -o pgid= -p $$ | tr -d ' ')"',"pcpu":98.0,"command":"python"}]' \
  LIVE_SPEC_OWNED_PGIDS="$(ps -o pgid= -p $$ | tr -d ' ')" \
  python3 guardrails/check-runaway-child.py
```

`LIVE_SPEC_OWNED_PGIDS` (space/comma-separated) and `LIVE_SPEC_OWNED_TREE` override the owned process
groups and owned temp tree; unset, the check owns its own process group and the repo's `.live-spec/`
tree. The check always exits zero, so the notice never blocks a stop.

## The worker-restore gate — a worker never restores a working tree with a git command (row 479)

`guardrails/check-worker-restore.py` reds when a worker run handed a shell one of the commands the
clause names. A worker runs no command that discards uncommitted work, in any tree: `git checkout --
<path>`, `git checkout .`, `git restore` outside `--staged`, `git stash` and its `push`, `save`,
`create` and `store` forms, `git reset` with `--hard`, `--merge` or `--keep`, and `git clean` with
`-f` or `-x`. Such a command's blast radius is a PATH, so its damage lands on files the worker never
wrote and its brief never named, and the write-set disjointness that fences concurrent edits gives
no cover against it. This rule binds a worker in every tree, including its own isolated worktree,
since a worktree shares one repository with the lanes beside it and a worker cannot read off its
brief what else that repository holds.

That list is stated in this section, in the gate's own header, and in `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md`,
`skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md`, `skills/build-pipeline/references/delegation-protocol.md`,
`templates/agent.template.md` and `scripts/open-lane.sh`, in one wording, and
`tests/test_worker_restore.py` reds when two of them differ.

The gate reds on this project's own sessions. The transcript root holds the owner's other projects too.
A discarding command in one of their sessions is their defect, as row 598 says in words.
The key is the session's recorded `cwd`: a session belongs to a neighbour when that directory exists
and git reads it as another repository. A session the gate cannot place elsewhere still reds. Only
where `cwd` alone answers nothing does the gate take one further look, at `effective_dir`. This is the
directory the one command actually ran in, once any `cd` inside it is walked — printed as `ran in`. An
owner's home directory (unplaceable) whose command `cd`ed into a real neighbouring checkout is that
neighbour's finding too (row 623). The look never overrides a `cwd` the key could already place. An
`effective_dir` that is itself `UNKNOWN` or unplaceable leaves the session reading as this project's
own, unchanged. The same holds when it lands back in this project's own repository — a sibling lane
worktree among them. A neighbour's finding is never dropped — it prints as a notice naming session,
directory, command and outcome, and reds nothing.

It opens the worker-run transcripts under the harness transcript root (`~/.claude/projects` by
default, `--root` or `LIVE_SPEC_TRANSCRIPT_ROOT` to move it): the files matching
`<project-dir>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`, one per worker run. In each it reads the
records whose `type` is `assistant` and takes the `input.command` string of every `tool_use` block
named `Bash`. It reads no prose — a report that merely names a restore is left alone, and only a
segment whose first word is `git` counts, so the same text quoted inside a `grep` pattern stays
silent. The default window is the runs touched in the last 24 hours (`--since-hours`, `--all` for
every run on disk).

Every finding says what the shell did with the command. The `tool_use` block carries an `id`. The
shell's answer sits in the same transcript as a `tool_result` block repeating it as `tool_use_id`.
A call the harness refused is marked there by a `toolDenialKind` key. Its four values are
`automode-blocked`, `permission-rule`, `user-rejected` and `interrupted`. A call that reached a
shell carries no such key, whatever its exit status.

So a finding reads one of three ways. The command ran. The harness declined it. Or the transcript
answers nothing, and the outcome is unknown. All three red, because the rule forbids handing such a
command to a shell at all. Whether the shell obeyed lies outside the worker's reach.

What the outcome tells the reader is how much recovery it faces. The findings print ranked by that:
the executed ones first, the unanswered ones second, the declined attempts last. The unanswered ones
outrank the declined because they cannot be ruled out. The verdict line tallies the three. The typed
JSON line carries `outcome`, an `outcomes` count, and the first finding after the ranking.
tlvphotos asked for this on 2026-08-12, in
`inbox/2026-08-12-tlvphotos-reply-worker-restore-finding.md`. It had received a finding that read as
lost work, when the classifier had declined the command and nothing was lost.

It is BLOCKING and rides the verify step rather than the push chain: a push gate runs long after the
bytes are gone, while verify is where the orchestrator accepts a worker's result. It is armed in two
places. `skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md` step 8 names the command a session runs before it accepts a
worker's result, and `tests/test_worker_restore.py` runs it against the machine's real transcript
root so a red reaches a person on the next suite run. When the transcript root does not exist the
gate stands down by name and exits zero; when the root exists but holds no worker-run transcript, the
layout it reads has moved and it reds by name through `guardrails/nonempty_input.py` rather than
reporting clean over nothing (SPEC INV-218).

The gate carries a counting start, `COUNTING_FROM` in its own header (`--counting-from`,
`LIVE_SPEC_WORKER_RESTORE_FROM`). This machine's transcripts hold worker runs from before the clause
existed that carry a discarding command. This page states no figure for that class, and no figure
would hold. The runs live in a transcript root outside this repository, and that root grows while a
person reads it. Two readings minutes apart returned different totals on 2026-08-06. Ask the machine
that holds them instead. The command
`python3 guardrails/check-worker-restore.py --counting-from 2000-01-01 --all` lists every such run on
this machine, with the date each one carries. A finding stamped before the counting start is carried
as history: every verdict line counts it and it reds nothing. A finding stamped on or after that date
reds, and so does a finding whose record carries no timestamp, since the gate cannot place it.

INV-176) — never only the diff. Pre-gate debt surfaces the day the gate lands; a backlog too
large to fold at once is absorbed by seeding the cap at the current size (SPEC INV-172).

neighbours' CLI lesson, adopted from OpenSpec's gate contract — provenance and the full

the queue archive):

   emits exactly one parseable JSON object — `{"severity": "...", "code": "...", "message": "...",

2. **Every check declares blocking or advisory.** A header comment names it; an advisory check

3. **All-or-nothing writes.** A script that rebuilds artifacts validates every output before writing any — no half-written artifact ever lands on disk.

reach) rather than a defect; it is a decider, informational rather than a blocking gate.

The gates' native home is the LOCAL pre-push hook — CI is the second net, never the first. Three
rules: **same checks, one source of truth** — CI invokes the same scripts in this directory

## The kill-list scanner (SPEC E-26)

A host with taste-reviewed artifacts keeps a kill-list beside them (template:
`templates/KILL_LIST.template.md` — the human's cuts as dated literals, appended, never removed) and
wires a SCANNER: a test that reads the kill-list table and greps the artifact's surfaces for each
literal — a killed phrase reappearing turns the suite red. Same shape as every gate here: the list is the
declared truth, the test re-walks it every run.

# Отчёт

Путь есть. Останавливаюсь, ничего не строю, дерево не менял, не коммитил, не пушил.

## Как он зовётся

Запустить `guardrails/pre-push` напрямую как обычный shell-скрипт, минуя `git push`:

```
bash guardrails/pre-push < /dev/null
```

Для полного набора, включая гейт b (пачку pytest, которую по умолчанию гоняет только сервер):

```
LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 bash guardrails/pre-push < /dev/null
```

## Почему это тот же набор и не пуш — улики

1. **Скрипт нигде не толкает наружу.** `grep -rn "git push\|git fetch\|curl \|wget \|ssh " guardrails/*.sh guardrails/*.py scaffold/guardrails/*.py` — ни одного вызова, кроме упоминания в комментарии `check-deletion-only-push.sh`. Хук — это чистая последовательность локальных проверок; git сам вызывает его перед сетевым обменом, а если вызвать руками — сети вообще не касаешься.
2. **Ручной вызов уже предусмотрен автором.** `guardrails/pre-push`, строки 16-24: код явно проверяет `[ -t 0 ]`, потому что «a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and must never block on a read». Это прямое указание, что ручной запуск — штатный сценарий.
3. **База диапазона одна и та же что в хуке, что вручную.** `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh` (строки 107-112) вообще не читает переданные git'ом ref-lines для базы — только `LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE` (при обычном локальном пуше он не задан) или `git rev-parse origin/main`. То же самое `origin/main` использует и `pre-push` для гейта g (строка 84) и для гейта h (`--base origin/main`, строка 272). Значит настоящий git-хук при реальном пуше и ручной вызов судят абсолютно один и тот же диапазон `origin/main..HEAD` одним и тем же кодом — это не «похожий» набор, а буквально тот же файл.

## Доказательство прогоном

Выполнил `bash guardrails/pre-push < /dev/null` в рабочей копии (дерево чистое, ветка = origin/main, диапазон пуст). Прошли все 27 быстрых гейтов из README (весь список кроме b), теми же строками `-- gate X: ... --` и `OK`/`FAIL`, что напечатал бы настоящий хук. В частности гейт h напечатал ровно:

```
OK (tests-present): no user-facing files changed against origin/main
```

— тот самый гейт, который координатор считал видимым только после попытки пуша с `LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1`. Финал: `All gates green — push allowed.`, exit=0. После прогона `git status` не изменился, ветка осталась «up to date with origin/main» — сеть не трогали.

## Почему координатор мог не увидеть

Судя по формулировке беды, гейты пробовали только через настоящий `git push` (или искали отдельный «dry» режим/цель), не пробуя вызвать файл `guardrails/pre-push` как обычный исполняемый скрипт напрямую из шелла. Хук выглядит как git-артефакт, который «умеет» запускаться только автоматически при пуше — но по факту это самостоятельный bash-файл без единого сетевого вызова, который можно дёргать вручную сколько угодно раз без всякого риска.

## Что осталось незакрытым

Ничего не построено и не нужно строить — задача решена констатацией существующего пути. Единственное, чего нет: явной строчки в `guardrails/README.md`, что `bash guardrails/pre-push` можно вызывать вручную как сухой прогон. Это отдельная, маленькая правка документации (не гейта), не относящаяся к запрету «строить новый гейт поверх существующего» — оставляю на ваше решение, нужна ли она вообще.
